name: Leucophyllum

project_scope.native_target_zone_status: UNRESOLVED; Texas state native, county certification pending

look_here_first: A WOODY, much-branched shrub with silver-gray soft densely hairy small leaves and single axillary tubular flowers. Count 5 corolla lobes and inspect four stamens; don't group with Salvia just because both are called Texas sage.
shared_traits: Woody xeric shrubs with simple, often gray pubescent leaves
Often solitary flowers in leaf axils rather than whorled/clustered Salvia flowers

comparison_matrix.Leucophyllum frutescens: Scrophulariaceae, persistent woody stem; small silvery tomentose leaves
comparison_matrix.Salvia texana: Lamiaceae, usually herbaceous mint stem, typically opposite non-silvery leaves
Racemose flowers, typically 2 fertile stamens, calyx and corolla differently arranged

comparison_matrix.Leucophyllum frutescens: Tube or bell-shaped lavender flower with broad lips; no spines
comparison_matrix.Solanum elaeagnifolium: Rotate/star-shaped lavender corolla with conspicuous yellow anther cone; may have prickles

comparison_matrix.Leucophyllum frutescens: Short entire ash-gray leaves; compare calyx and flower, wild provenance important
comparison_matrix.Cultivated or related Leucophyllum: Several overlap, and many nursery plants are cultivars; no cultivar photo counts as local genotype or indigenous population

visual_photo_sequence.where: Observe overall woody crown, not a sheared nursery ball
Trace gray small blades to leaf bases; true hairs need later macro

visual_photo_sequence.show: Texas branch with open axillary flower
visual_photo_sequence.where: Note silver leaf clusters and pink tubular corolla; out-of-focus background is non-diagnostic
Find funnel tube and 5 lobes, next check for four stamens

visual_photo_sequence.show: real close-up corolla and dried old fruit
visual_photo_sequence.where: Examine tubular five-lobed corolla and adjacent older brown fruit; use species text to learn four-stamen structure. Ripe capsule valves are not sufficiently exposed to certify dehiscence.

cautions: Cultivar names Green Cloud, Compacta and other horticultural clones do not certify wild-type provenance
Hays iNaturalist observation flag does not prove native range
Photo arrows must wait for actual installed image review and verified target coordinates

curation_status.stage: canonical species installed with five physically verified images
curation_status.remaining: calibrated diagnostic structures and county range validation

visual_comparison.title: Cenizo — Silver leaves, axillary flowers, and woody shrub
visual_comparison.subtitle: Five physically installed and source-attributed photos; one South Texas park location, the others photographed in cultivation outside Texas. Provenance never equals target-zone native certification.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Silver woolly LEAVES + WOODY shrub + SINGLE tubular flowers from LEAF AXILS = CENIZO. Not Salvia texana.

items.label: Silver-gray small leaves
items.image_role: Small crowded gray obovate to elliptic leaves; the foliage's tomentum causes silver appearance
items.caption: Look for the uniformly pale, soft leaf surfaces. Follow each blade to its short shoot to understand clustered attachment. Real trichome shapes need higher-magnification macro.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr

items.label: Texas flowering branch
items.image_role: Pink-purple flowers with adjacent ash-colored leaves on branch
items.caption: See the small leaf clusters and lavender tubular flowers. Photo taken in a Texas state park, but documented location alone is not proof of an indigenous wild population.
items.creator: cricketsblog (Melissa McMasters)
items.photo_status: PHYSICAL_IMAGE_VERIFIED; photo center and foreground are clearer than upper background

items.label: Flower and older fruit close-up
items.image_role: Five-lobed purple-pink flower, silver leaves, and old brown fruit
items.caption: This close-up is best for learning the corolla lobes and observing the stem and old fruit together. Do not claim visible capsule dehiscence or stamen-count accuracy without a dissected macro.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr

items.label: Flowering branches overview
items.image_role: Dense gray foliage with many small pink flowers; NOT a flower close-up
items.caption: Recognize the pink flush across silver branches. The actual image shows many flowers rather than any single flower's inner parts.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr

items.label: Whole shrub habit
items.image_role: Full habit of a planted cenizo bush, natural uneven branch shapes
items.caption: This cultivated specimen demonstrates size, crown shape and dense silver foliage; it does not document natural growth habitat in target counties.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr
